text: Filtering to the Southeast — the exact region the Sales Director asked about back in lesson one — the drill-down page shows a churn rate of 9.8%, nearly double the company-wide 4.1% baseline.

An aggregate number can hide a cause that isn't spread evenly at all, and stopping at the region level would be a mistake here, so the next step is cutting one level deeper, down to individual stores.

A store-level query reveals two specific locations, Eastland Commons and Riverwatch Crossing, account for roughly 320 of the Southeast's 510 churned customers. That's about 63% of the region's entire churn, from just two of its several stores.

Both locations recently lost a neighboring anchor tenant, a documented driver of reduced foot traffic for the smaller retailers left behind. That's a checkable external fact, not a guess, and it's worth confirming with the regional manager before calling it the cause.

The finding gets re-stated at the right altitude: this isn't a Southeast-wide problem, and it's definitely not a company-wide one. It's two storefronts that lost foot traffic, while the rest of the region performs close to normal.

That distinction changes everything that happens next — a narrow, cheap fix for two stores, not an expensive company-wide retention campaign the data never actually supported. Next up: delivering this finding to the Sales Director herself.
